## The Print

Apple's FY2025 revenue rose 6.4% to $416.2B, with net income up 19.5% to $112.0B and diluted EPS up 22.7% to $7.46.

Revenue growth accelerated from 2.0% in FY2024 to 6.4% in FY2025, with Services becoming a larger share of total sales and Greater China revenue declining 3.8%.

- Total net sales increased 6.4% YoY to $416.2B, driven by Services growth of 13.5% and iPhone growth of 4.2%.
- Net income increased 19.5% YoY to $112.0B, reflecting a lower effective tax rate (15.6% vs 24.1%) and higher operating income.
- Diluted EPS increased 22.7% YoY to $7.46, aided by a 2.6% reduction in weighted-average diluted shares outstanding.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net sales | $416,161M | $391,035M | +6.4% | Increase driven by higher net sales of iPhone, Services, Mac and iPad, partially offset by lower Wearables, Home and Accessories. |
| Products net sales | $307,003M | $294,866M | +4.1% | Increase driven by higher iPhone and Mac sales, partially offset by lower Wearables, Home and Accessories. |
| Services net sales | $109,158M | $96,169M | +13.5% | Increase primarily due to higher net sales from advertising, the App Store and cloud services. |
| Gross margin | $195,201M | $180,683M | +8.0% | Increase driven by higher total net sales and a higher gross margin percentage. |
| Operating income | $133,050M | $123,216M | +8.0% | Increase driven by higher gross margin, partially offset by higher operating expenses. |
| Net income | $112,010M | $93,736M | +19.5% | Increase driven by higher operating income and a lower effective tax rate. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $7.46 | $6.08 | +22.7% | Increase driven by higher net income and a lower share count. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of $133.1B was driven by core operations. The effective tax rate of 15.6% benefited from a $10.7B year-over-year decrease in the provision for income taxes related to the State Aid Decision, which had inflated the prior year's tax expense. Excluding this one-time item, the tax rate would have been higher.

Operating cash flow was 1.0x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $98.8B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $15.4B (prior $15.2B), share repurchases $90.7B (prior $94.9B); capital expenditures $12.7B (prior $9.4B).

Apple continued its aggressive capital return program, repurchasing $89.3B of common stock and paying $15.4B in dividends. The company also issued $4.5B in new term debt, maintaining a net debt position despite large buybacks.

Return on equity was 151.9% (prior 164.6%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 31.2% (prior 25.7%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In May 2025, the Company announced a new share repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26 per share beginning in May 2025.

## Forward Signals

The Company did not provide quantitative guidance for the next fiscal year. Management noted that gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure due to various factors, including tariffs.

**Known trends**
- Tariffs and other trade measures announced in 2025 could materially adversely affect the Company's business, results of operations and financial condition, including impacting supply chain, pricing and gross margin.

> "The Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tariffs and trade restrictions could increase costs, limit component availability, and require supply chain changes, adversely affecting results. | Beginning in the second quarter of 2025, new tariffs were announced on imports to the U.S. (“U.S. Tariffs”), including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the European Union (“EU”), among others. |
| 2 | Dependence on single or limited sources for critical components exposes the company to supply shortages and price increases. | Because the Company currently obtains certain components from single or limited sources, the Company is subject to significant supply and pricing risks. |
| 3 | Intense competition in global markets could pressure margins and market share. | The Company’s products and services are offered in highly competitive global markets. These markets are characterized by aggressive price competition, downward pressure on gross margins, continual improvement in product performance, and price sensitivity on the part of consumers and businesses. |
| 4 | Legal proceedings and government investigations, including patent claims, could result in significant damages or injunctive relief. | The Company has faced and continues to face a significant number of patent claims relating to its standards-enabled products, and new claims may arise in the future. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Americas | $178.4B | $72.5B | +6.8% | 41% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone and Services, with unfavorable foreign currency impact. |
| Europe | $111.0B | $47.7B | +9.6% | 43% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of Services, iPhone and Mac. |
| Greater China | $64.4B | $26.9B | -3.8% | 42% operating margin — Net sales decreased primarily due to lower net sales of iPhone, partially offset by higher net sales of Mac. |
| Rest of Asia Pacific | $33.7B | $14.6B | +9.9% | 43% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and Mac. |
| Japan | $28.7B | $14.0B | +14.6% | 49% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and iPad. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (term debt + commercial paper) was $98.7B, while cash and marketable securities totaled $132.4B, resulting in a net cash position of $33.7B. Shareholders' equity was $73.7B.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $132.4B provide substantial liquidity. The company also has access to debt markets and an undrawn commercial paper program.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $111.5B, investing $15.2B, financing $-120.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $148.0B vs. current liabilities $165.6B (current ratio 0.89x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-09-28: $153.0B vs. $176.4B (0.87x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- As of September 27, 2025, $12.4B of term debt is payable within 12 months.
- The company has $8.0B of commercial paper outstanding, payable within 12 months.

## The Print

Microsoft's FY2025 revenue rose 15% to $281.7B, with net income up 16% to $101.8B and diluted EPS up 16% to $13.64, driven by 34% growth in Azure and other cloud services.

Revenue grew 15% and operating income grew 17%, with Intelligent Cloud leading growth at 21% revenue increase, while gross margin percentage decreased slightly due to scaling AI infrastructure.

- Revenue increased 15% to $281.7B, with growth across all three segments.
- Net income increased 16% to $101.8B, and diluted EPS increased 16% to $13.64.
- Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9B, with Azure and other cloud services revenue growing 34%.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $281.7B | $245.1B | +14.9% | Revenue increased $36.6 billion or 15% with growth across each of our segments. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure. Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. More Personal Computing revenue increased driven by Gaming and Search and news advertising. |
| Gross margin | $193.9B | $171.0B | +13.4% | Gross margin increased $22.9 billion or 13% with growth across each of our segments. Gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by Intelligent Cloud, offset in part by More Personal Computing. |
| Operating income | $128.5B | $109.4B | +17.5% | Operating income increased $19.1 billion or 17% with growth across each of our segments. |
| Net income | $101.8B | $88.1B | +15.6% | Net income increased 16% to $101.8 billion. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $13.64 | $11.80 | +15.6% | Diluted earnings per share increased 16% to $13.64. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of $128.5B is driven by core segment performance. Other income (expense), net was a loss of $4.9B, primarily reflecting net recognized losses on equity method investments, including OpenAI, and higher impairments on investments. Net income includes these non-operating items, but they are not material relative to operating income.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $71.6B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $24.1B (prior $21.8B), share repurchases $18.4B (prior $17.3B); capital expenditures $64.6B (prior $44.5B).

Microsoft continues to return significant capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases while investing heavily in AI and cloud infrastructure. The company increased dividends paid and maintained a substantial share repurchase program, with $57.3B remaining under authorization. Capital expenditures rose sharply to support cloud and AI growth, funded primarily by operating cash flow.

Return on equity was 29.6% (prior 32.8%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 16.5% (prior 17.2%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- As of June 30, 2025, $57.3 billion remained of our $60 billion share repurchase program.
- During fiscal years 2025 and 2024, our Board of Directors declared dividends totaling $24.7 billion and $22.3 billion, respectively.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide specific quantitative guidance for fiscal 2026. Management discusses continued investment in cloud and AI infrastructure and expects operating costs to increase, which may decrease operating margins.

**Known trends**
- The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins.
- We continue to identify and evaluate opportunities to expand our datacenter locations and increase our server capacity to meet the evolving needs of our customers, particularly given the growing demand for AI services.

**Subsequent events**
- The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) was enacted on July 4, 2025, providing a U.S. global intangible low-taxed income effective tax rate of 14% effective fiscal year 2027 for Microsoft.

> "The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins." — Management

We are incurring significant costs to build and maintain infrastructure to support cloud-based and AI services, reducing operating margins. |
| 3 | Cyberattacks and security vulnerabilities could lead to reduced revenue, increased costs, liability claims, or harm to reputation. | Cyberattacks and security vulnerabilities could lead to reduced revenue, increased costs, liability claims, or harm to our reputation or competitive position. |
| 4 | The IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest related to transfer pricing for tax years 2004-2013. | In the NOPAs, the IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest. |

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Productivity and Business Processes | $120.8B | $69.8B | +13.1% | 58% operating margin — Revenue increased driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, with Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue up 14% and LinkedIn revenue up 9%. |
| Intelligent Cloud | $106.3B | $44.6B | +21.5% | 42% operating margin — Revenue increased driven by Azure, with Azure and other cloud services revenue growing 34%. |
| More Personal Computing | $54.6B | $14.2B | +7.5% | 26% operating margin — Revenue increased driven by Gaming and Search and news advertising, with Xbox content and services revenue up 16% and search and news advertising ex-TAC up 20%. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (short-term + long-term) was $43.2B as of June 30, 2025, down from $51.6B a year earlier. Cash and short-term investments totaled $94.6B, resulting in a net cash position of $51.4B. Shareholders' equity increased to $343.5B from $268.5B.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $94.6B as of June 30, 2025, up from $75.5B. Management expects existing cash, investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to be sufficient to fund operating activities and cash commitments for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $136.2B, investing $-72.6B, financing $-51.7B.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

NVIDIA reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B, up 85% YoY, with net income of $58.3B and diluted EPS of $2.39.

Revenue, net income, and EPS all more than doubled year-over-year, with gross margin up 14.4 percentage points.

- Revenue increased 85% YoY to $81.6B, driven by Data Center demand for Blackwell 300 and networking solutions.
- Net income rose 211% YoY to $58.3B, with diluted EPS of $2.39, up 214% YoY.
- Gross margin expanded to 74.9% from 60.5% a year ago, primarily due to the absence of a $4.5B H20 inventory charge.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $81,615M | $44,062M | +85.2% | Driven by data center products for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with Blackwell accounting for the majority of system shipments. |
| Gross profit | $61,157M | $26,668M | +129.3% | Gross margin increased primarily due to the prior year's $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations. |
| Operating income | $53,536M | $21,638M | +147.4% | Operating income growth was driven by higher revenue and the non-recurrence of the H20 charge. |
| Net income | $58,321M | $18,775M | +210.6% | Net income growth was driven by higher operating income and a $16.1B increase in other income, primarily from unrealized gains on equity investments. |
| Diluted EPS | $2.39 | $0.76 | +214.5% | EPS growth outpaced net income growth due to a lower share count from repurchases. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of $53.5B was driven by core operations, while net income included $15.9B of other income, primarily unrealized gains on publicly-held and non-marketable equity securities. Excluding these gains, net income would have been significantly lower.

Operating cash flow was 0.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $48.6B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $243.0M (prior $244.0M), share repurchases $19.3B (prior $14.1B); capital expenditures $1.8B (prior $1.2B).

The company continued aggressive share repurchases and increased its dividend, funded by strong operating cash flow.

Return on equity was 29.8% (prior 22.4%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 22.5% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Board approved an additional $80.0B share repurchase authorization on May 18, 2026.
- Quarterly dividend increased from $0.01 to $0.25 per share, payable June 26, 2026.

## Forward Signals

No specific financial guidance was provided in the filing.

**Known trends**
- Rubin platform expected to start shipping in the second half of fiscal year 2027.
- Data center, energy, and capital availability constraints could impact future revenue.

**Subsequent events**
- On May 18, 2026, the Board approved an additional $80.0B share repurchase authorization and increased the quarterly dividend to $0.25 per share.

> "We expect our Rubin platform to start shipping in the second half of fiscal year 2027." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Competition from customers developing their own ASICs and other competitors could reduce demand for NVIDIA products. | Some of our customers are developing their own ASICs and other products, including designs optimized for certain workloads that may not require all of the features and functionality our data center systems provide. |
| 2 | Supply chain and demand estimation risks could lead to inventory provisions or lost revenue. | If we overestimate demand, or if customers cancel or defer orders or choose to purchase from our competitors, we may not be able to utilize on-hand inventory or reduce purchase commitments accordingly. |
| 3 | Export controls and geopolitical tensions could limit sales to China and other markets. | The United States has imposed unilateral worldwide controls restricting GPUs and associated products, and it is likely that additional unilateral or multilateral controls will be adopted. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compute & Networking | $74.5B | $53.3B | +88.3% | 72% operating margin — Year-over-year revenue growth driven by Data Center products, including Blackwell systems and networking solutions. |
| Graphics | $7.1B | $2.9B | +57.9% | 42% operating margin — Year-over-year revenue growth driven by sales of Blackwell architecture. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt of $8.47B (including short-term portion) against cash and marketable securities of over $80B; net cash position is substantial.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable debt securities totaled $50.3B, plus $30.2B of marketable equity securities; management believes liquidity is sufficient for at least the next 12 months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $50.3B, investing $-26.4B, financing $-21.3B.

Working capital: Current assets $151.0B vs. current liabilities $43.9B (current ratio 3.44x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2026-01-25: $125.6B vs. $32.2B (3.91x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- No commercial paper outstanding under the $25.0B program.
- Complied with non-financial covenants on outstanding notes.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Investment commitments | Total investment commitments were $27B as of April 26, 2026, expected to be made through the remainder of fiscal year 2027. |
| Manufacturing, supply, and capacity commitments | Commitments totaled $119B, with $95B to be paid in the remainder of fiscal year 2027. |
| Facility lease guarantee | Maximum gross exposure under facility lease guarantees is $3.5B, reduced by partner payments and $712M in escrow. |

## The Print

JPMorgan Chase reported net income of $57.0B for 2025, down 2% YoY, with diluted EPS of $20.02 and total net revenue of $182.4B, up 3%.

Revenue grew modestly, but net income declined due to higher provision for credit losses and noninterest expense.

- Total net revenue increased 3% to $182.4B, driven by higher net interest income and noninterest revenue.
- Net income decreased 2% to $57.0B, while diluted EPS increased 1% to $20.02 due to share repurchases.
- Provision for credit losses rose 33% to $14.2B, including a $2.2B addition related to the Apple Card transaction.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net Interest Income | $95,443,000,000 (2025-12-31) | $92,583,000,000 (2024-12-31) | — |  |
| Non-Interest Income | $87,004,000,000 (2025-12-31) | $84,973,000,000 (2024-12-31) | — |  |
| Total net revenue | $182,447M | $177,556M | +2.8% | Driven by higher net interest income and noninterest revenue, including higher Markets revenue and asset management fees. |
| Provision for credit losses | $14,212M | $10,678M | +33.1% | Net charge-offs of $9.8B and net addition to allowance of $4.4B, including $2.2B related to Apple Card transaction and loan growth in Card Services. |
| Total noninterest expense | $95,640M | $91,797M | +4.2% | Higher compensation expense, brokerage expense, distribution fees, auto lease depreciation, technology and marketing investments, partially offset by FDIC special assessment releases and absence of Visa contribution. |
| Income before income tax expense | $72,595M | $75,081M | −3.3% | Decrease due to higher provision for credit losses and noninterest expense, partially offset by higher revenue. |
| Income tax expense | $15,547M | $16,610M | −6.4% | Effective tax rate decreased to 21.4% from 22.1%, driven by a $774M tax benefit from audit resolutions and tax regulations, and higher tax benefits from share-based awards. |
| Net income | $57,048M | $58,471M | −2.4% | Decrease driven by higher provision for credit losses and noninterest expense, partially offset by higher revenue and lower tax expense. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $20.02 | $19.75 | +1.4% | Increase despite lower net income due to reduction in weighted-average diluted shares from 2,879.0M to 2,781.5M. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Coca-Cola reported Q1 2026 net income of $3.924B ($0.91 diluted EPS) on revenue of $12.472B, up 12% YoY.

Revenue and operating income grew double digits, while operating cash flow turned positive after a prior-year outflow.

- Revenue increased 12% YoY to $12.472B, driven by 8% concentrate sales volume growth and favorable price/mix.
- Net income rose 18% YoY to $3.924B, with diluted EPS up 18% to $0.91.
- Operating cash flow swung to $2.021B from -$5.202B in the prior-year quarter, reflecting improved working capital.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net Operating Revenues | $12,472M | $11,129M | +12.1% | Increase driven by 8% concentrate sales volume growth, favorable price/mix of 2%, and favorable foreign currency impact of 3%, partially offset by acquisitions/divestitures of -1%. |
| Gross Profit | $7,852M | $6,966M | +12.7% | Gross profit margin increased to 63.0% from 62.6%, primarily due to favorable pricing initiatives, foreign currency, and the sale of Nigeria finished product operations, partially offset by higher commodity costs. |
| Operating Income | $4,359M | $3,659M | +19.1% | Increase driven by higher concentrate sales volume, favorable price/mix, lower operating expenses, lower other operating charges, and favorable foreign currency, partially offset by increased marketing spending and higher commodity costs. |
| Net Income Attributable to Shareowners of The Coca-Cola Company | $3,924M | $3,330M | +17.8% | Increase driven by higher operating income and lower effective tax rate, partially offset by lower other income. |
| Diluted Net Income Per Share | $0.91 | $0.77 | +18.2% | Increase consistent with higher net income; share count remained relatively flat. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income included $21M of other operating charges (vs $73M prior year), primarily related to indemnification agreements, modernization initiatives, and tax litigation expense. Other income (loss) — net was $21M, including a $10M impairment charge on Africa bottling operations held for sale and $13M of factoring costs, compared to $254M prior year which included a $331M gain on CCEP sale.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $1.8B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $2.3B (prior $89.0M), share repurchases $477.0M (prior $370.0M); capital expenditures $266.0M (prior $309.0M).

Capital allocation priorities remain investing in the business, growing dividends, enhancing portfolio through acquisitions, and repurchasing shares to offset dilution. The company expects 2026 capex of approximately $2.2B and plans share repurchases to offset stock-based compensation dilution.

Return on equity was 11.7% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 3.8% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- The company expects 2026 capital expenditures to be approximately $2.2 billion.
- During 2026, the company expects to repurchase shares to offset dilution resulting from employee stock-based compensation.

## Forward Signals

The company expects foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations to have a favorable impact on full year 2026 net operating revenues and operating income. The effective tax rate for 2026 is expected to be approximately 19.9% before considering significant operating and nonoperating items.

**Known trends**
- Sales of ready-to-drink beverages are somewhat seasonal, with the second and third calendar quarters typically accounting for the highest sales volumes.
- The company remains subject to global trade dynamics, which may impact certain components of its cost structure and consumer sentiment.

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Ongoing IRS tax litigation for tax years 2007-2009 could result in a material cash outflow if the company does not prevail on appeal. The Tax Court entered a decision reflecting additional federal income tax of $2.7 billion, and with interest the total liability is $6.0 billion, which the company paid as a deposit in September 2024. | On August 2, 2024, the Tax Court entered a decision reflecting additional federal income tax of $2.7 billion for the 2007 through 2009 tax years. With applicable interest, the total liability for the 2007 through 2009 tax years resulting from the Tax Court’s decision is $6.0 billion, for which the IRS issued the Company invoices on September 3, 2024. |
| 2 | The BodyArmor trademark impairment of $960 million recorded in Q4 2025 indicates potential for further impairment if near-term operating results do not meet revised projections or macroeconomic conditions worsen. | If the near-term operating results of this trademark do not achieve our revised financial projections, or if the macroeconomic conditions change, causing the discount rate to increase without an offsetting increase in the operating results, it is likely that we would be required to recognize an additional impairment charge. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| North America | $4.9B | $1.6B | +12.2% | 33% operating margin — Unit case volume increased 4%, driven by 5% growth in Trademark Coca-Cola and water, sports, coffee and tea; operating income rose on higher concentrate sales volume and favorable price/mix. |
| EMEA | $3.0B | $1.3B | +13.4% | 42% operating margin — Unit case volume increased 2%, with growth in sparkling flavors and water, sports, coffee and tea, partially offset by a 15% decline in juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverages due to the Nigeria divestiture. |
| Latin America | $1.7B | $1.0B | +13.6% | 62% operating margin — Unit case volume increased 1%, with growth in water, sports, coffee and tea and sparkling flavors; operating income benefited from higher concentrate sales volume and favorable price/mix. |
| Bottling investments | $1.6B | $191.0M | +12.1% | 12% operating margin — Unit case volume increased 1%, primarily driven by growth in Africa, partially offset by the impact of refranchising certain territories in India. |
| A. Pacific | $1.5B | $536.0M | +6.1% | 36% operating margin — Unit case volume increased 5%, with broad-based growth across categories; operating income declined due to unfavorable price/mix and higher commodity costs. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (loans and notes payable plus current maturities of long-term debt plus long-term debt) was $43.9B as of April 3, 2026, compared to $45.5B at December 31, 2025. Cash and cash equivalents were $10.6B, resulting in net debt of approximately $33.3B.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and marketable securities totaled $13.8B as of April 3, 2026. The company also had $6.6B in unused backup lines of credit for general corporate purposes.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $2.0B, investing $1.7B, financing $-3.9B.

Working capital: Current assets $30.4B vs. current liabilities $22.4B (current ratio 1.36x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-12-31: $31.0B vs. $21.3B (1.46x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Current maturities of long-term debt increased to $4.5B from $1.8B at December 31, 2025.
- The company has $6.6B in unused backup lines of credit expiring at various times through 2031.

| Supply Chain Finance Program | The company had $1,262 million of confirmed obligations outstanding under the supply chain finance program as of April 3, 2026, down from $1,363 million at December 31, 2025. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Tesla's 2025 revenue fell 2.9% to $94.8B while net income attributable to common stockholders dropped 46.5% to $3.79B, as automotive sales declined and regulatory credit revenue shrank.

Revenue and profitability declined year-over-year, with automotive sales and regulatory credits down while energy storage and services grew.

- Total revenue decreased $2.86B to $94.83B, driven by a 9% decline in automotive sales revenue.
- Net income attributable to common stockholders fell to $3.79B from $7.09B, with diluted EPS down to $1.08 from $2.04.
- Energy generation and storage revenue grew 27% to $12.77B, partially offsetting automotive weakness.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $94,827M | $97,690M | −2.9% | Decrease driven by lower automotive sales revenue, partially offset by growth in energy generation and storage and services. |
| Automotive sales | $65,821M | $72,480M | −9.2% | Decrease due to approximately 8% lower cash deliveries and lower average selling price per unit driven by sales mix and higher customer incentives. |
| Automotive regulatory credits | $1,993M | $2,763M | −27.9% | Decrease due to governmental and regulatory actions, such as OBBBA, restricting certain regulatory credit programs. |
| Energy generation and storage revenue | $12,771M | $10,086M | +26.6% | Increase primarily due to higher Megapack and Powerwall deployments, partially offset by lower average selling price of Megapack. |
| Services and other revenue | $12,530M | $10,534M | +18.9% | Increase primarily due to higher paid Supercharging sessions, non-warranty maintenance services, used vehicle sales volume, and automotive insurance revenue. |
| Gross profit | $17,094M | $17,450M | −2.0% | Decrease primarily due to lower automotive gross profit, partially offset by higher energy generation and storage gross profit. |
| Income from operations | $4,355M | $7,076M | −38.5% | Decrease driven by higher operating expenses, particularly R&D and SG&A, and lower gross profit. |
| Net income attributable to common stockholders | $3,794M | $7,091M | −46.5% | Decrease due to lower operating income and unfavorable other income, partially offset by lower tax provision. |
| Diluted EPS | $1.08 | $2.04 | −47.1% | Decrease consistent with lower net income, partially offset by higher weighted average diluted shares. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of $4.36B included $494M in restructuring and other charges, primarily related to AI chip design convergence ($390M) and prior-year restructuring. Net income also reflected a $419M other expense, driven by bitcoin mark-to-market and FX losses, versus a $695M gain in 2024.

Operating cash flow was 3.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $6.2B.

**Red flag:** Automotive regulatory credits revenue declined 28% due to regulatory changes, a high-margin revenue stream that may continue to shrink.

**Red flag:** R&D expense increased 41% to $6.41B, outpacing revenue growth and compressing operating margin.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $8.5B (prior $11.3B).

Capital expenditures decreased to $8.53B from $11.34B, but management expects capex to exceed $20B in 2026, driven by AI initiatives and manufacturing expansion. The company continues to prioritize growth investments over shareholder returns, with no dividends or buybacks disclosed.

Return on equity was 4.6% (prior 9.7%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 2.8% (prior 5.8%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Management expects capital expenditures to exceed $20 billion in 2026, driven by AI initiatives, including investments in compute infrastructure and data centers.

## Forward Signals

Management expects capital expenditures to exceed $20 billion in 2026, driven by AI initiatives, manufacturing expansion, and growth in company-operated AI-enabled assets. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

**Known trends**
- Rapidly evolving trade and fiscal policy, including tariffs, poses risks to global supply chain and cost structure, with a relatively larger impact on the energy generation and storage business.
- The OBBBA's removal of tax credits for electric vehicles may impact consumer demand for EVs.

**Subsequent events**
- In January 2026, the Company entered into an agreement to make a minority equity investment in xAI.

> "We currently expect our capital expenditures to be in excess of $20 billion in 2026, driven by our AI initiatives, including investments in compute infrastructure and data centers, the expansion and ramp of our manufacturing and R&D production lines and facilities, and growth in our fleet of company-operated AI-enabled assets and our retail, service and charging footprint." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Dependence on Elon Musk, who does not devote full time to Tesla and holds management positions at other companies. | We are highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer. Although Mr. Musk spends significant time with Tesla and is highly active in our management, he does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla. |
| 2 | Supply chain risks, including reliance on single-source suppliers and battery cell suppliers like Panasonic and CATL. | Our products contain thousands of parts purchased globally from hundreds of suppliers, including single-source direct suppliers, which exposes us to multiple potential sources of component shortages. |
| 3 | Tariffs and trade policy changes could increase costs and reduce demand, particularly for energy storage products. | The current tariff regime will have a relatively larger impact on our energy generation and storage business compared to our automotive business. |
| 4 | Product liability and regulatory scrutiny related to autonomous driving and vehicle safety. | Such collisions, whether involving Robotaxi vehicles or customer vehicles with driver assistance features engaged, are often subject of significant public attention, especially in light of NHTSA’s Standing General Order requiring reports regarding certain crashes involving vehicles with advanced driver assistance or autonomous driving systems. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Automotive segment | $82.1B |  | -6.3% | Automotive sales revenue declined due to lower deliveries and average selling price, while regulatory credit revenue fell sharply on regulatory changes. Gross margin for total automotive decreased from 18.4% to 17.8%. |
| Energy generation and storage segment | $12.8B |  | +26.6% | Revenue grew 27% on higher Megapack and Powerwall deployments, and gross margin expanded from 26.2% to 29.8% due to lower raw material and manufacturing costs, partially offset by higher tariffs. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt and finance leases (current and non-current) were $8.38B, against cash and cash equivalents of $16.51B and short-term investments of $27.55B, resulting in a net cash position of approximately $35.7B.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents plus short-term investments totaled $44.06B at year-end, with $6.43B of unused committed credit amounts. Management believes current sources of funds provide adequate liquidity for at least the next 12 months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $14.7B, investing $-15.5B, financing $1.1B.

Working capital: Current assets $68.6B vs. current liabilities $31.7B (current ratio 2.16x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: $58.4B vs. $28.8B (2.02x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- As of December 31, 2025, $1.58B of debt is current, with total minimum lease payments of $7.96B, of which $1.32B is due within 12 months.

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| 2025 CEO Performance Award | Unrecognized stock-based compensation expense of $10.23B for probable operational milestone and $105.82B to $120.37B for not probable milestones, to be recognized over up to 9.7 years. |
| Automotive Warranty Reserve | Total accrued warranty was $8,607 million as of December 31, 2025, primarily related to the automotive segment, with estimates based on actual claims and projected future costs. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Amazon's 2025 revenue rose 12% to $716.9B, with net income up 31% to $77.7B and diluted EPS up 30% to $7.17.

Revenue growth accelerated to 12% from 11% in 2024, while net income growth slowed to 31% from 95% in 2024, and free cash flow dropped sharply due to higher capital expenditures.

- Revenue increased 12% to $716.9B, driven by AWS growth of 20% and North America growth of 10%.
- Net income rose 31% to $77.7B, with diluted EPS up 30% to $7.17.
- Free cash flow fell 71% to $11.2B as capital expenditures nearly doubled to $128.3B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net sales | $716,924M | $637,959M | +12.4% | Sales increased 12% in 2025, compared to the prior year. |
| Operating income | $79,975M | $68,593M | +16.6% | Operating income was $68.6 billion and $80.0 billion for 2024 and 2025. |
| Net income | $77,670M | $59,248M | +31.1% | Net income increased 31% in 2025, compared to the prior year. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $7.17 | $5.53 | +29.7% | Diluted earnings per share increased 30% in 2025, compared to the prior year. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of $80.0B included $2.5B for an FTC lawsuit settlement, $2.7B of severance costs, and $1.3B of asset impairments. Other income (expense), net of $15.2B included a $7.2B upward adjustment for Anthropic preferred stock and $5.6B of reclassification gains on Anthropic convertible notes, which are non-operating and non-cash.

Operating cash flow was 1.8x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $7.7B.

**Red flag:** Free cash flow fell 71% to $11.2B despite net income rising 31%, driven by a 65% increase in capital expenditures to $128.3B.

**Red flag:** Other income (expense), net swung from -$2.3B to +$15.2B, driven by unrealized gains on Anthropic investments, which may not be recurring.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $131.8B (prior $83.0B).

Capital expenditures nearly doubled to $128.3B, primarily for technology infrastructure to support AWS growth, funded by operating cash flow and $15.7B of new long-term debt. No dividends or share repurchases were disclosed.

Return on equity was 18.9% (prior 20.7%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 9.5% (prior 9.5%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

## Forward Signals

First quarter 2026 net sales are expected to be between $173.5B and $178.5B, or to grow between 11% and 15% compared with first quarter 2025. Operating income is expected to be between $16.5B and $21.5B, compared with $18.4B in first quarter 2025.

**Known trends**
- Management expects spending in technology and infrastructure to increase over time, including to support artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives.
- Management expects capital expenditures to increase in 2026, primarily for technology infrastructure to support AWS business growth.

**Subsequent events**
- Subsequent to December 31, 2025, an additional portion of Anthropic convertible notes was converted to nonvoting preferred stock, resulting in a gain of approximately $3B to be recorded in Q1 2026, and an upward adjustment of approximately $12B to the nonvoting preferred stock.

> "We expect spending in technology and infrastructure will increase over time, which can negatively impact short-term free cash flow, as we add infrastructure and employees, including to support our artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives, to support long-term growth." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Intense competition across all business segments, including e-commerce, cloud services, and advertising, could reduce sales and profits. | Our businesses are rapidly evolving and intensely competitive, and we have many competitors across geographies, including cross-border competition, and in different industries, including physical, e-commerce, and omnichannel retail, e-commerce services, web and infrastructure computing services, electronic devices, digital content, advertising, grocery, healthcare, communications, and transportation and logistics services. |
| 2 | International operations expose the company to regulatory, economic, and geopolitical risks, particularly in China and India, which could disrupt operations. | The People’s Republic of China (“PRC”) and India regulate Amazon’s and its affiliates’ businesses and operations in country through regulations and license requirements that may restrict (i) foreign investment in and operation of the internet, IT infrastructure, data centers, retail, delivery, and other sectors, (ii) internet content, and (iii) the sale of media and other products and services. |
| 3 | Significant fluctuations in operating results and growth rate due to seasonality, macroeconomic conditions, and other factors. | We Experience Significant Fluctuations in Our Operating Results and Growth Rate |
| 4 | Risks related to optimizing and operating fulfillment network and data centers, including capacity mismatches and labor constraints. | Failures to adequately predict customer demand and consumer spending patterns or otherwise optimize and operate our fulfillment network and data centers successfully from time to time result in excess or insufficient fulfillment or data center capacity, service interruptions, increased costs, and impairment charges, any of which could materially harm our business. |
| 5 | Data loss or security incidents could expose the company to liability and harm its reputation. | Because we collect, process, store, and transmit large amounts of data, including confidential, classified, sensitive, proprietary, and business and personal information, failure to prevent, detect, or mitigate data loss, theft, misuse, unauthorized access, or other security incidents or vulnerabilities affecting our or our vendors’ or customers’ technology, products, and systems, could: expose us or our customers to a risk of loss, disclosure, or misuse of such information; adversely affect our operating results; result in litigation, liability, or regulatory action. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| North America | $426.3B | $29.6B | +10.0% | 7% operating margin — Sales growth primarily reflects increased unit sales, including sales by third-party sellers, advertising sales, and subscription services, driven by focus on price, selection, and convenience. |
| International | $161.9B | $4.8B | +13.3% | 3% operating margin — Sales growth primarily reflects increased unit sales, including sales by third-party sellers, advertising sales, and subscription services, driven by focus on price, selection, and convenience. |
| AWS | $128.7B | $45.6B | +19.7% | 35% operating margin — Sales growth primarily reflects increased customer usage, partially offset by pricing changes primarily driven by long-term customer contracts. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (long-term debt of $65.6B plus current portion) versus cash and marketable securities of $123.0B results in a net cash position. Shareholders' equity increased to $411.1B from $286.0B.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $123.0B at year-end 2025, up from $101.2B. The company also has two unsecured revolving credit facilities and commercial paper programs with no borrowings outstanding.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $139.5B, investing $-142.5B, financing $9.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $229.1B vs. current liabilities $218.0B (current ratio 1.05x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: $190.9B vs. $179.4B (1.06x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt increased to $65.6B from $52.6B, with $15.7B of new long-term debt issued in 2025.

## The Print

ExxonMobil's 2025 revenue declined 5.0% to $332.2B, net income fell 14.4% to $28.8B, and diluted EPS decreased 14.5% to $6.70.

Lower crude oil prices and divestments reduced revenue and earnings, while higher capital expenditures and lower operating cash flow compressed free cash flow.

- Revenue decreased 5.0% to $332.2B, driven by lower crude prices and divestments.
- Net income declined 14.4% to $28.8B, with diluted EPS down 14.5% to $6.70.
- Operating cash flow fell 5.5% to $52.0B, while capital expenditures rose 16.7% to $28.4B, reducing free cash flow 23.1% to $23.6B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sales and other operating revenue | $323,905M | $339,247M | −4.5% | Management attributes the decline to lower crude prices and divestments. |
| Total revenues and other income | $332,238M | $349,585M | −5.0% | Management attributes the decline to lower crude prices and divestments. |
| Net income (loss) attributable to ExxonMobil | $28,844M | $33,680M | −14.4% | Management attributes the decline to lower crude prices and divestments. |
| Earnings (loss) per common share - assuming dilution (dollars) | $6.70 | $7.84 | −14.5% | Management attributes the decline to lower crude prices and divestments. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Management discloses identified items of $(893)M in Upstream for 2025, primarily asset impairments, compared to a $215M gain in 2024. Energy Products identified items were $483M gain in 2025, mainly from asset sales.

Operating cash flow was 1.8x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $23.6B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $17.2B (prior $16.7B), share repurchases $20.3B (prior $19.6B); capital expenditures $28.4B (prior $24.3B).

Management continues to return significant cash to shareholders through dividends and buybacks, while increasing capital expenditures to fund advantaged growth projects in the Permian, Guyana, and LNG.

Return on equity was 11.1% (prior 12.8%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 6.4% (prior 7.4%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

## Forward Signals

Management expects to increase Permian production to approximately 2.5 Moebd by 2030 and anticipates eight FPSO vessels in operation on the Stabroek Block by year-end 2030.

**Known trends**
- Management expects a shift in the geographic mix and type of opportunities from which volumes are produced, with the proportion of oil-equivalent production from the Americas generally increasing over the next several years.

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A material decline in oil or natural gas prices could have a material adverse effect on operations, results, financial condition, and proved reserves, especially in the Upstream segment. | Any material decline in oil or natural gas prices could have a material adverse effect on the Company’s operations, results, financial condition, and proved reserves, especially in the Upstream segment. |
| 2 | Geopolitical issues could disrupt transportation of Kazakhstan oil through the CPC pipeline, potentially causing a loss of cash flows of uncertain duration from operations in Kazakhstan. | In the event geopolitical issues escalate in the region, including ongoing military conflict, it is possible that the transportation of Kazakhstan oil through the CPC pipeline could be disrupted, curtailed, temporarily suspended, or otherwise restricted. |
| 3 | Government actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, such as carbon taxes or restrictive permitting, could increase compliance costs and reduce demand for hydrocarbons. | Government actions intended to reduce greenhouse gas emissions include adoption of cap and trade regimes, carbon taxes, carbon accounting, carbon-based import duties or other trade tariffs, minimum renewable usage requirements, restrictive permitting, increased mileage and other efficiency standards, mandates for sales of electric vehicles, restrictions on sales of gasoline-only vehicles, mandates for disclosure of plans to reduce emissions or reduce the use or production of certain products, mandates for use of specific fuels or technologies, and other incentives or mandates designed to support certain technologies for transitioning to lower-emission energy sources. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (notes and loans payable plus long-term debt) was $43.5B at year-end 2025, down from $41.7B at year-end 2024. Cash and cash equivalents were $10.7B, resulting in a net debt position of $32.8B.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents decreased to $10.7B from $23.0B, primarily due to share repurchases and dividends exceeding operating cash flow after capital expenditures.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $52.0B, investing $-25.9B, financing $-39.1B.

Working capital: Current assets $83.4B vs. current liabilities $72.3B (current ratio 1.15x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: $92.0B vs. $70.3B (1.31x).

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Pfizer reported Q1 2026 revenue of $14.5B, up 5% YoY, while net income fell 9% to $2.7B ($0.47 diluted EPS).

Revenue growth resumed, but profitability declined due to higher cost of sales and R&D expenses, and a higher effective tax rate.

- Total revenues increased 5% to $14.5B, driven by growth in Padcev, Eliquis, Oncology biosimilars, and Nurtec ODT/Vydura, partially offset by declines in COVID-19 products.
- Net income attributable to Pfizer Inc. common shareholders decreased 9% to $2.7B, with diluted EPS of $0.47 compared to $0.52 in the prior-year quarter.
- Operating cash flow increased 12% to $2.6B, while free cash flow rose 23% to $2.2B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $14,451M | $13,715M | +5.4% | Operational increase of 2% plus favorable foreign exchange impact of 3%, driven by Padcev, Eliquis, Oncology biosimilars, Nurtec ODT/Vydura, partially offset by COVID-19 product declines. |
| Net income attributable to Pfizer Inc. common shareholders | $2,687M | $2,967M | −9.4% | Decrease primarily due to higher cost of sales and R&D expenses, partially offset by lower restructuring charges and higher revenues. |
| Diluted EPS | $0.47 | $0.52 | −9.6% | Reflects lower net income and slightly higher diluted share count. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income includes $137M of acquired in-process R&D expenses, $100M of restructuring charges and acquisition-related costs, and a $295M unfavorable change in contingent consideration liabilities. Excluding these items, operating performance was stronger than reported.

Operating cash flow was 1.0x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $2.2B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $2.4B (prior $2.4B); capital expenditures $436.0M (prior $564.0M).

Pfizer continued to return capital to shareholders through dividends ($2.4B paid) while reducing debt and investing in R&D and acquisitions. The company's capital allocation reflects a balance between shareholder returns and strategic investments.

Return on equity was 3.0% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 1.3% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Completed acquisition of Metsera in November 2025 for $8.0B, expanding obesity and cardiometabolic pipeline.
- Entered into commercialization collaboration with Sciwind Biosciences for ecnoglutide in Mainland China, with up to $495M in milestone payments.
- Completed exit of ViiV investment on March 31, 2026, receiving $1.875B in cash proceeds.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide updated full-year guidance; management references the 2025 Form 10-K outlook and notes expected unfavorable revenue impact from patent expiries of approximately $1.5B in 2026.

**Known trends**
- Anticipated significant reduction of revenue from patent-based or regulatory exclusivity expiries in 2026 through 2030, with acceleration expected.
- Pricing and access pressures from governments and payors, including IRA Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program impacts on Eliquis effective January 1, 2026.

**Subsequent events**
- On March 31, 2026, Pfizer completed the exit of its 11.7% investment in ViiV, receiving $1.875B in cash proceeds.

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Patent expiries and loss of exclusivity expected to reduce revenue by approximately $1.5B in 2026, with acceleration through 2030. | We anticipate a significant reduction of revenue from patent-based or regulatory exclusivity expiries in 2026 through 2030 as several of our in-line products experience these expirations, with the rate of the reduction of revenues from patent-based or regulatory exclusivity expiries expected to significantly accelerate over the next few years. In 2026, we continue to expect an unfavorable revenue impact from patent-based or regulatory exclusivity expiries of approximately $1.5 billion. |
| 2 | Government pricing and access pressures, including IRA Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program, impacting Eliquis effective January 1, 2026, with Ibrance and Xtandi to follow in 2027. | We continue to monitor and evaluate the implementation of the IRA, including the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program (MDPNP) and its government-set Maximum Fair Price which became effective for Eliquis on January 1, 2026. Negotiated prices for Ibrance and Xtandi are expected to follow in 2027, with Xeljanz effective in 2028. |
| 3 | Potential impact of Section 232 tariffs on imported patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients, up to 100% duty, phasing in July 31, 2026, subject to negotiation. | Specifically, on April 2, 2026, the U.S. Government announced Section 232 tariffs on imported patented pharmaceuticals and their ingredients, up to a 100% duty to address national security concerns regarding supply chain reliance. These measures, featuring exemptions for commitments to onshore and invest in U.S. manufacturing, are set to phase in on July 31, 2026, and the application to Pfizer is subject to the final negotiation of our tariff agreement with the U.S. Government. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (short-term borrowings + long-term debt) was $64.5B as of March 29, 2026, down from $64.8B at December 31, 2025. Cash and cash equivalents were $1.7B, with short-term investments of $11.4B, providing ample liquidity.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of $1.7B plus short-term investments of $11.4B, along with operating cash flow of $2.6B, provide sufficient liquidity. No credit facility details disclosed in this filing.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $2.6B, investing $785.0M, financing $-2.9B.

Working capital: Current assets $42.8B vs. current liabilities $34.3B (current ratio 1.25x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-12-31: $42.9B vs. $37.0B (1.16x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Current portion of long-term debt was $3.9B as of March 29, 2026.
- No covenant breaches or material debt maturities disclosed in this filing.

| In-Licensing Arrangement with Sciwind Biosciences | Obtained exclusive commercialization rights for ecnoglutide in Mainland China, with up to $495M in milestone payments. |
| Sale of ViiV Investment | Completed exit of 11.7% investment in ViiV on March 31, 2026, receiving $1.875B in cash proceeds. |

## The Print

Ford reported Q1 2026 net income of $2.55B ($0.63 diluted EPS) on revenue of $43.25B, up 6.4% YoY.

Net income increased $2.08B YoY, primarily due to higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT and higher Ford Credit EBT, partially offset by higher taxes and special item charges.

- Revenue increased 6.4% YoY to $43.25B, driven by higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT.
- Net income rose to $2.55B from $473M a year ago, with diluted EPS of $0.63 versus $0.12.
- Company adjusted EBIT was $3.49B, up from $1.02B, reflecting improved segment profitability.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $43,253M | $40,659M | +6.4% | Increase driven by higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT, as stated in MD&A. |
| Operating income | $2,329M | $319M | +630.1% | Increase driven by higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT and higher Ford Credit EBT. |
| Net income attributable to Ford Motor Company | $2,548M | $471M | +441.0% | Increase driven by higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT and higher Ford Credit EBT, partially offset by higher taxes and special item charges. |
| Diluted EPS | $0.63 | $0.12 | +425.0% | Increase driven by higher net income. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income includes $226M of pre-tax special item charges, primarily restructuring in Europe and EV program cancellations, partially offset by pension and OPEB remeasurement gains. Company adjusted EBIT was $3,488M, excluding these special items.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $-1.1B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $607.0M (prior $1.2B), share repurchases $311.0M; capital expenditures $2.4B (prior $1.8B).

Ford maintained its dividend at $0.15 per share (down from $0.30 including supplemental dividend in Q1 2025) and repurchased $311M of common stock under its anti-dilutive share repurchase program. Capital spending increased to $2.38B from $1.82B, reflecting continued investment in product development and electrification.

Return on equity was 6.8% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 0.9% (prior 0.2%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Settled $2.3B 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes in cash and issued 6.6 million shares of Ford Common Stock held as treasury stock to settle the conversion premium, which were subsequently repurchased as part of the anti-dilutive share repurchase program.

## Forward Signals

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Walmart's fiscal 2026 revenue reached $713.2B, up 4.7% YoY, with net income attributable to Walmart of $21.9B and diluted EPS of $2.73.

Revenue growth moderated slightly from 5.1% in fiscal 2025 to 4.7% in fiscal 2026, while net income growth accelerated due to a $2.1B net gain on investments and higher operating income.

- Total revenues increased 4.7% to $713.2B, driven by comparable sales growth across U.S. segments and international markets.
- Consolidated net income attributable to Walmart rose 12.6% to $21.9B, with diluted EPS up 13.3% to $2.73.
- Operating cash flow increased 14.1% to $41.6B, while free cash flow grew 17.9% to $14.9B despite higher capital expenditures.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $713,163M | $680,985M | +4.7% | Increase primarily due to strong positive comparable sales across U.S. segments and international markets, with growth in average ticket and transactions. |
| Operating income | $29,825M | $29,348M | +1.6% | Increase driven by higher gross profit and membership income, partially offset by higher operating expenses including self-insured claims and PhonePe share-based compensation charge. |
| Net income attributable to Walmart | $21,893M | $19,436M | +12.6% | Increase primarily due to a $2.1B net gain on investments (vs. $0.8B loss in prior year) and higher operating income. |
| Diluted EPS | $2.73 | $2.41 | +13.3% | Increase reflects higher net income and lower share count due to repurchases. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income includes a $2.1B net gain on investments (vs. $0.8B loss in prior year) and a $0.7B non-cash charge for PhonePe share-based compensation modification. Excluding these items, operating income grew modestly, with operating margin declining 13bps to 4.2%.

Operating cash flow was 1.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $14.9B.

**Red flag:** Operating margin declined 13bps to 4.2% despite revenue growth, driven by higher self-insured general liability claims expense ($0.9B) and PhonePe share-based compensation charge ($0.7B).

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $7.5B (prior $6.7B), share repurchases $8.1B (prior $4.5B); capital expenditures $26.6B (prior $23.8B).

Capital allocation remained balanced, with increased capex focused on supply chain, technology, and customer-facing initiatives, while shareholder returns accelerated through higher dividends and share repurchases. The company funded these primarily through operating cash flow and modest debt issuance.

Return on equity was 22.0% (prior 21.4%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 7.7% (prior 7.5%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In February 2026, the Board approved a new $30.0B share repurchase authorization, replacing the remaining $4.0B under the prior program.
- Effective February 19, 2026, the annual dividend was increased to $0.99 per share from $0.94 per share.

## Forward Signals

For fiscal 2027, Walmart projects capital expenditures of approximately $25B to $27B, with a focus on technology, supply chain, and customer-facing initiatives.

**Known trends**
- Management expects continued uncertainty due to tariffs, inflation, currency fluctuations, and supply chain pressures, with less than one third of U.S. merchandise imported.

**Subsequent events**
- In February 2026, the Board approved a new $30.0B share repurchase authorization and a dividend increase to $0.99 per share for fiscal 2027.

> "We expect continued uncertainty in our business and the global economy due to the following factors: tariffs and trade restrictions; inflationary trends; fluctuations in global currencies; swings in macroeconomic conditions and their effect on consumer confidence; changes in employment trends; volatility in fuel prices; and supply chain pressures, any of which may impact our results." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Failure to successfully execute omnichannel strategy and cost of eCommerce/technology investments could materially adversely affect market position, net sales, and financial performance. | Failure to successfully execute our omnichannel strategy and the cost of our investments in eCommerce and technology may materially adversely affect our market position, net sales and financial performance. |
| 2 | Strong competition from other retailers, wholesale club operators, and omnichannel retailers could materially adversely affect financial performance. | We face strong competition from other retailers, wholesale club operators, omnichannel retailers and other businesses which could materially adversely affect our financial performance. |
| 3 | General or macro-economic factors, including inflation, higher interest rates, and tariffs, may materially adversely affect financial performance. | General or macro-economic factors, both domestically and internationally, may materially adversely affect our financial performance. |
| 4 | Cybersecurity incidents or failure to maintain privacy/security of information could damage reputation, result in litigation, fines, and materially adversely affect business. | Any failure to maintain the privacy or security of the information relating to our company, customers, members, associates, business partners and vendors, whether as a result of cyberattacks on our information systems or otherwise, could damage our reputation, result in litigation or other legal actions against us, result in fines, penalties, and liability, cause us to incur substantial additional costs and materially adversely affect our business and operating results. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Walmart U.S. | $485.6B | $25.2B | +4.4% | 5% operating margin |
| Walmart International | $132.0B | $5.1B | +7.0% | 4% operating margin — Net sales growth of 7.0% was driven by positive comparable sales across international markets, including strong eCommerce growth of $6.3B, partially offset by negative currency fluctuations of $2.8B. |
| Sam's Club U.S. | $95.5B | $2.4B | +3.2% | 3% operating margin |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (short-term borrowings + long-term debt) was $44.8B at year-end, with cash and cash equivalents of $10.7B, resulting in net debt of $34.1B. Shareholders' equity was $99.6B, yielding a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.45x.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of $10.7B, supplemented by $15.0B in undrawn committed lines of credit and strong operating cash flow of $41.6B, provide ample liquidity for operations, investments, dividends, and share repurchases.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $41.6B, investing $-26.4B, financing $-13.6B.

Working capital: Current assets $84.9B vs. current liabilities $107.5B (current ratio 0.79x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-01-31: $79.5B vs. $96.6B (0.82x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt maturities: $3.5B due within one year, $3.2B in fiscal 2028, $3.4B in fiscal 2029, $2.1B in fiscal 2030, $2.6B in fiscal 2031, and $23.3B thereafter.
- Committed lines of credit mature in April 2026 and April 2030, with covenants including a maximum secured debt restriction.

| Contingencies - legal proceedings | Company is involved in various legal proceedings and regulatory matters, including opioid-related litigation, Asda Equal Value Claims, and antitrust matters; potential losses are disclosed when reasonably possible. |

## The Print

Costco reported net income of $2,192 million ($4.93 diluted EPS) on total revenue of $70,527 million for the third quarter of fiscal 2026, with net sales up 12% year-over-year.

Net sales growth accelerated to 12% from 8% in the prior-year quarter, aided by higher gasoline prices and favorable foreign currency, while membership fee revenue growth of 11% reflected fee increases and new sign-ups.

- Total revenue increased 11.6% to $70,527 million, driven by a 12% increase in net sales and an 11% increase in membership fees.
- Net income rose 15.2% to $2,192 million, with diluted EPS up 15.2% to $4.93.
- Comparable sales increased 10% overall, with digitally-enabled comparable sales up 21%.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenue | $70,527 million | $63,205 million | +11.6% | Net sales increased 12% driven by comparable sales growth and new warehouses, while membership fees increased 11%. |
| Operating income | $2,815 million | $2,530 million | +11.3% | Operating income increased due to higher gross margin dollars and lower SG&A as a percentage of net sales. |
| Net income | $2,192 million | $1,903 million | +15.2% | Net income increased on higher operating income and a lower effective tax rate. |
| Diluted EPS | $4.93 | $4.28 | +15.2% | Diluted EPS growth matched net income growth as share count remained relatively flat. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating results were clean, with no material one-time items. Gross margin benefited from a smaller LIFO charge and the absence of a one-time vacation expense, while SG&A benefited from the absence of that same vacation charge.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Costco continues to return capital to shareholders through dividends and buybacks while investing in expansion. The dividend was increased 13% year-over-year, and the company repurchased $603 million of stock in the first thirty-six weeks. Capital expenditures of $4,228 million are funding new warehouses and digital capabilities.

Return on equity was 6.5% (prior 7.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 2.5% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Quarterly cash dividend increased to $1.47 per share from $1.30 per share in the prior-year quarter.
- Board authorized a $4,000 million share repurchase program expiring January 2027, with $1,359 million remaining.

## Forward Signals

Management intends to spend approximately $6,500 million on capital expenditures in fiscal 2026 and plans to open 13 additional new warehouses (including one relocation) in the remainder of the fiscal year.

**Known trends**
- Higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve results, per management.

## The Print

Boeing swung to a net profit of $2.2B in 2025 from a $11.8B loss in 2024, with revenue up 34.5% to $89.5B, driven by higher commercial deliveries and a $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture.

Boeing returned to profitability in 2025 after two consecutive annual losses, driven by a $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture, higher commercial deliveries, and lower defense program charges.

- Revenue increased 34.5% to $89.5B, primarily on higher commercial airplane deliveries.
- Net income attributable to Boeing shareholders was $2.2B, versus a loss of $11.8B in 2024.
- Diluted EPS was $2.48, compared with a loss of $18.36 per share in 2024.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $89,463M | $66,517M | +34.5% | Revenues increased by $22,946 million in 2025 compared with 2024 primarily driven by higher revenues at BCA, BDS and BGS. BCA revenues increased by $18,633 million primarily due to higher deliveries. |
| Net earnings/(loss) attributable to Boeing shareholders | $2,235M | $(11,817)M | +118.9% | Earnings from operations increased by $14,988 million in 2025 compared with 2024, primarily driven by BGS ($9,856 million), BDS ($5,285 million) and BCA ($890 million), partially offset by an increase in loss from operations on Unallocated items, eliminations and other ($984 million). |
| Diluted earnings/(loss) per share | $2.48 | $(18.36) | +113.5% | Diluted earnings per share increased to $2.48 from a loss of $18.36, reflecting the return to profitability and a higher diluted share count of 762.3 million versus 646.9 million. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported earnings from operations of $4,281M include a $9,672M gain on dispositions, primarily the $9,566M gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture. Excluding this gain, core operating earnings were $3,236M, still a significant improvement from the prior-year core operating loss of $11,811M. The gain is non-recurring and flatters the operating margin; underlying operations remain loss-making at BCA and BDS.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $-1.9B.

**Red flag:** BCA segment loss from operations was $7,079M in 2025, driven by $5,283M of combined reach-forward losses on the 777X and 767 programs.

**Red flag:** Free cash flow was negative $1,877M in 2025, despite the return to net profitability, indicating continued cash consumption in operations.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $331.0M; capital expenditures $2.9B (prior $2.2B).

Capital allocation in 2025 was dominated by the $10.55B all-cash Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture and the $8.4B Spirit AeroSystems acquisition (funded largely with $4.7B of Boeing stock). The company paid $331M in mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends and made no common stock repurchases. Capital expenditures rose to $2,942M, up from $2,230M, reflecting continued investment in production capacity. The divestiture proceeds strengthened liquidity, but the acquisition and ongoing negative free cash flow indicate a focus on strategic repositioning over shareholder returns.

Return on equity was 41.0% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 1.3% (prior -7.6%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Completed the $10.55B all-cash sale of portions of the Digital Aviation Solutions business to Thoma Bravo on October 31, 2025.
- Completed the acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc. on December 8, 2025, for total consideration of $8,371M, including $4,704M in Boeing common stock.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide quantitative financial guidance for 2026. Management discusses expectations for production rate increases (737 to 47 per month in 2026, 787 to 8 per month), certification of the 737-7 and 737-10 in 2026, and first delivery of the 777-9 in 2027, but does not give revenue or earnings guidance.

**Known trends**
- Management expects the 737 production rate to increase from 42 to 47 per month in 2026 with FAA concurrence, and is planning additional increases beyond 47.
- The 777X program continues to face certification and production challenges, with first delivery of the 777-9 delayed to 2027 and additional reach-forward losses possible.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 23, 2026, the Commerce, Justice Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 6938) was enacted, funding certain federal departments and agencies, including NASA, through FY26.

> "We continue to expect first delivery of the 777-9 to occur in 2027." — Management
